_readme: Built by scripts/build-desk.py. Real series come from EIA daily spot (and NYMEX gas via Yahoo); modeled series are straight lines between cited anchors and say so. Do not edit by hand.

cards.title: Colonial Pipeline shutdown, May 2021
cards.open: The East Coast's fuel pipe just went dark.
cards.why: Colonial carries ~45% of East Coast fuel. When it shut, the only way north was Jones Act tankers, so freight, not the barrel spread, captured the dislocation. EIA spot shows the NYH-Gulf gasoline spread widening only ~$2/bbl while MR earnings jumped to ~$50k/day.
cards.source: EIA daily spot NYH and USGC conventional gasoline; S&P Global (13 May 2021) Jones Act MR ~$50k/day; Colonial Pipeline statements 7-15 May 2021.

nyh_usgc.label: NYH − USGC gasoline
nyh_usgc.source: EIA daily spot: NYH minus USGC conventional gasoline, $/gal × 42

jones_mr.label: Jones Act MR tanker

anchors.source: Assumption: pre-shutdown Jones Act MR level (no public daily print)
Assumption: Colonial shut late on May 7
S&P Global, 13 May 2021: Jones Act MR TCE ~$50,000/day USGC-New York on May 12, per a Jones Act broker
Assumption: brokers expected rates to ease once the line restarted (S&P Global, 13 May 2021)

jones_mr.source: Modeled: straight lines between the dated anchors listed (each cited).

steps.headline: Gulf gasoline $2.23/bbl under New York
steps.text: Colonial moves ~2.5 MMb/d of fuel from Houston to Linden. The spread is roughly its tariff.

steps.title: Ship Gulf gasoline to New York on a Jones Act MR
steps.pitch: Buy 300k bbl at Houston, fix a US-flag MR for 8 days, sell NY Harbor on arrival. Spread $3.15 vs ~$1.40 to move it.
killers: Flat price drops while you're on the water: this is unhedged
Freight spikes before you fix the ship
NYH premium collapses when the line restarts

steps.headline: Colonial shuts all 5,500 miles after ransomware attack
steps.text: The East Coast's main fuel artery is down. Every Jones Act product tanker on the Gulf gets booked.

steps.title: Scheduler: your Cycle 27 line space
steps.prompt: 150k bbl nominated Houston → Linden can't move. Hold the nomination for the restart, or release it and sell at Houston?

options.label: Hold nomination, keep barrels in tank

later.text: Line restarted; your 150k bbl shipped and sold NYH

options.label: Release it, sell at Houston now

now.text: Sold at Houston spot: no spread, no tankage

later.text: Line restarted without you: missed the cycle

steps.title: Charter a Jones Act MR for 30 days
steps.pitch: The pipe is down; ships are the only way north. Take an MR on time charter now and relet it as rates climb.
killers: The line restarts fast and every charterer cancels
Jones Act waivers let foreign ships in
You can't find a relet: you're stuck paying hire

steps.headline: Colonial restarts; full service in days
steps.text: Fuel starts moving again late May 12. Panic buying left gas stations dry across the Southeast.

steps.title: Scheduler: berth at Linden
steps.prompt: Your MR arrives into a queue. Pay $40k to jump to an open berth, or wait out a 2-day line?

later.calc: 2 days × $50k/day (Jones Act MR rate that week)

steps.headline: Spread ends at $4.28: the ships, not the pipe, set the price
steps.text: Gulf to NY gasoline widened ~$2/bbl. Freight took most of it.

cards.title: Winter Storm Uri, February 2021
cards.open: Texas is freezing. Gas cash is vertical.
cards.why: Uri froze wells, pipes and refineries at once. Henry Hub spot went from $3.76 to $23.86 and back to $3.16 in eight sessions while NYMEX futures barely moved: storage you could actually withdraw was the asset. Diesel cracks widened as ~6 MMb/d of refining went offline.
cards.source: EIA daily spot (Henry Hub RNGWHHD, WTI RWTC, USGC ULSD); NYMEX gas front month via Yahoo; IHS Markit (Feb 2021) ~6 MMb/d refining affected; Reuters/Argus Midland differentials.

ng_fut.source: NYMEX natural gas front-month settle (Yahoo Finance NG=F)

hh_fut.label: Henry Hub spot − futures

steps.headline: Arctic blast heads for Texas
steps.text: Forecasts show single digits in Midland and Houston. Gas demand for heat will spike.

steps.title: Pull your gas out of storage, sell it today
steps.pitch: You hold 1 Bcf at a Gulf salt cavern. Spot pays more than March futures: sell spot, buy the futures back.
killers: Pipes freeze and you can't deliver what you sold
Spot goes higher tomorrow: you sold too early
Futures spike and your buyback costs more

steps.headline: ERCOT blackouts; ~6 MMb/d of refining offline
steps.text: IHS Markit: Storm Uri hit nearly 6 million b/d of US refining. Permian wells freeze.

steps.title: Scheduler: Midland → Cushing nomination
steps.prompt: Nominations due 10am. You hold 50k b/d of line space, but frozen wells give you ~20k b/d.

later.text: Ship-or-pay on 30k b/d you couldn't fill
Line history cut 15%: less space next month

steps.title: Long the Gulf diesel crack
steps.pitch: Refineries froze; diesel will be short when demand comes back. Buy USGC ULSD vs WTI.
killers: Refineries restart faster than expected
Crude rallies faster than diesel
Demand stays frozen with the roads

steps.headline: Henry Hub cash prints $23.86
steps.text: Spot gas at Henry Hub hits $23.86/MMBtu while March futures sit near $3.20.

steps.title: Buy Midland, ship to Cushing
steps.pitch: Permian is frozen, Cushing looks cheap. Buy Midland, pay the tariff, sell Cushing in 3 days (hedged).
killers: Midland trades at a premium: the arb runs the wrong way
Wells thaw and Midland sags
Line space is prorated

steps.headline: Thaw: Henry Hub back at $3.16
steps.text: Spot gas collapses back to the futures. Refineries restart over the next weeks.

cards.title: Keystone leak, December 2022
cards.open: Keystone just shut. Hardisty is backing up.
cards.why: The December 2022 leak blew WCS out $6 in a day, but the move faded within a week while the line stayed shut: refiners and traders found other routes and the January discount barely moved. The panic discount was the trade, not the outage.
cards.source: WTI: EIA daily spot RWTC. WCS: Reuters 8 and 13 Dec 2022 (CalRock), Argus/S&P Global Dec 2022; Houston WCS and rail costs are labeled assumptions.

wcs.label: WCS Hardisty vs WTI

Reuters, 8 Dec 2022: Dec WCS at Hardisty $33.50 under WTI (CalRock)
Reuters, 13 Dec 2022: WCS $29.25 under WTI (CalRock)
Assumption: back within its range (Argus: 'within a well-worn range')

steps.headline: WCS steady around $27 under WTI
steps.text: Heavy Canadian crude flows south on Keystone, 622k b/d to Cushing and the Gulf.

steps.headline: Keystone shut after ~14,000 bbl leak in Kansas
steps.text: TC Energy halts the line. Heavy barrels back up at Hardisty.

steps.title: Scheduler: 50k bbl stranded at Hardisty
steps.prompt: Your December Keystone barrels can't move. Rent tank and wait, or dump them at today's panic discount?

later.text: Sold at ~−$29.25 after two weeks of tank

steps.title: Buy WCS at −$33.50
steps.pitch: The discount blew out $6 in a day on a leak, not on demand. Buy the differential, hedged on WTI, and wait for it to snap back.
killers: Keystone stays down for months (2017 outage pushed WCS past −$30 for months)
Alberta storage fills and producers dump
Refiners switch to Latin heavy grades

steps.title: Rail heavy crude to the Gulf
steps.pitch: Hardisty is $22 under Houston. Rail costs ~$17. Book cars and move 100k bbl to the coast.
killers: The spread narrows before your cars load
No rail cars on short notice
Keystone restarts and Hardisty snaps back

steps.title: Scheduler: Keystone restarts the Wood River leg
steps.prompt: Line space offered on the unaffected segment. Pay $1.50/bbl to jump the queue for your 50k bbl?

later.text: Moved before the January roll: saved tank and roll

steps.headline: WCS back near −$28.50
steps.text: The panic premium fades even with Keystone still partly shut.

cards.title: SPR release weeks, June 2022
cards.open: Policy barrels are hitting the Gulf.
cards.why: The 2022 SPR release was mostly sour crude, delivered into the Gulf. Commercial sour grades had to make room: Mars went from about −$4 to −$8.25 under WTI, its weakest since 2008, before refiners bought the discount.
cards.source: EIA daily spot (RWTC, RBRTE) and weekly SPR stocks (WCSSTUS1); Reuters 10 Jun 2022 and S&P Global 13 Jun 2022 Mars assessments; DOE SPR release history. Freight and blending values are labeled assumptions.

mars.label: Mars vs WTI

anchors.source: Assumption: early-June Mars discount
Reuters, 10 Jun 2022: Mars $6.50 under WTI, widest since March 2020
S&P Global: Mars assessed $8.25 under cash WTI on 13 Jun 2022, weakest since Oct 2008
Assumption: Mars steadies after the low (Reuters, June 2022)

mars.source: Modeled: straight lines between the dated anchors listed (each cited).

brent_wti.source: EIA daily spot RBRTE minus RWTC

steps.headline: SPR is releasing 1 MMb/d for six months
steps.text: The largest release in SPR history, ~180 MMbbl, mostly sour crude, into Gulf Coast refineries.

steps.title: Short Mars vs WTI
steps.pitch: Policy barrels are sour and they keep coming. Sell Mars vs WTI and buy it back once refiners are full.
killers: SPR sales slow or get cancelled
A coker restart soaks up sour barrels
OPEC cuts sour supply

steps.headline: SPR down 7.3 MMbbl in a week
steps.text: EIA's weekly data: commercial sour barrels pile up along the Gulf.

steps.title: Scheduler: pick a load window
steps.prompt: Your 500k bbl WTI export cargo to Rotterdam. Load June 8-10, or June 15-17 on a ship $150k cheaper?

later.text: Loaded; Brent−WTI $6.95 vs $6.58 when you chose
Loaded; Brent−WTI $8.22 vs $6.58 when you chose

steps.title: Export WTI to Europe
steps.pitch: Brent−WTI is ~$7. Buy WTI at the Gulf, ship to Rotterdam on an Aframax, sell against Brent.
killers: Brent−WTI narrows before you discharge
Freight rallies (2022 Aframax rates were extreme)
Flat price falls: unhedged cargo

steps.headline: Mars hits −$8.25, weakest since 2008
steps.text: S&P Global: sour grades from Mars to WCS are swamped by SPR barrels.

steps.title: Scheduler: blend to a refinery spec
steps.prompt: A refiner pays $0.75/bbl over formula for 1.5% sulfur. Blend 200k Mars with 100k Midland at $0.20/bbl?

steps.headline: Mars steadies near −$7
steps.text: Refiners load up on cheap sour. The policy discount starts to look like a bargain.

cards.title: Red Sea diversions, January 2024
cards.open: Ships are going the long way round.
cards.why: Diversions around the Cape add up to two weeks per Middle East-Europe voyage. That soaks up tanker capacity: LR2 earnings roughly doubled in a month while Brent-WTI barely moved. Owning ships (or charters) beat owning barrels.
cards.source: EIA daily spot (RBRTE, RWTC, NYH and USGC ULSD); S&P Global Jan 2024 LR2 freight reports; FreightWaves/Clarksons; BRS Cape fuel estimate; Argus war-risk premiums.

steps.headline: Houthi attacks push tankers away from Bab el-Mandeb
steps.text: Owners start routing Europe-bound cargoes around the Cape: up to two extra weeks a voyage.

steps.title: Take an LR2 on 60-day time charter
steps.pitch: Longer voyages soak up ships. Hire an LR2 now at ~$43k/day and relet it once the diversions bite.
killers: A ceasefire reopens Suez
Owners reposition ballast ships and add supply
Refinery runs drop in Europe, fewer cargoes

steps.headline: US and UK strike Houthi targets
steps.text: Dozens of tankers divert overnight. Europe-bound LR2 freight jumps 25% in four days (S&P Global).

steps.prompt: Your chartered tanker is approaching the Red Sea. Pay war-risk cover and transit, or go round the Cape?

steps.title: Long NY Harbor diesel vs the Gulf
steps.pitch: European diesel to New York gets pricier with every diversion. Buy NYH vs USGC ULSD.
killers: Gulf barrels just ship north on Colonial
Mild weather caps heating oil demand
Europe keeps its own diesel

steps.title: WTI export arb to Europe
steps.pitch: Brent−WTI widened toward $7. Sell WTI into Europe, but freight is up too.
killers: Brent−WTI narrows
Freight keeps climbing
Flat price drops: unhedged

steps.headline: LR2s earn ~$92k/day, near four-year highs
steps.text: Tonne-miles, not barrels, are the shortage: the same oil now needs more ship-days.
